routes.title: Attach a safety evidence gate to IndiaAI subsidised compute approvals
routes.impactRationale: Unscored new candidate; legacy numbers are compatibility placeholders and must not be shown.
routes.feasibilityRationale: Unscored new candidate; legacy numbers are compatibility placeholders and must not be shown.
routes.actor: IndiaAI Independent Business Division within Digital India Corporation, acting through its policy and PMEC approval process.
routes.obligor: An already-verified end-user company requesting more than 5,000 subsidised GPU-hours for model development, with its selected empanelled cloud provider implementing agreed access controls.
routes.instrument: End-User Policy sections 4.6 and 5.1–5.2: project/subsidy approval and policy updates; proposed prospective safety schedule in the allocation and provider/user terms.
routes.safeguard: For a defined high-capability pilot cohort, require a misuse evaluation plan before allocation, model-version-linked evaluation results before deployment, incident notification and a named person authorised to suspend the workload. This is a new proposed condition.
routes.verification: Proposed: retain approval IDs, model hashes, test protocols and review decisions; reconcile provider metering with the same allocation IDs. By 21–22 June 2027, test a simulated serious incident and show whether access suspension and corrective retesting actually occurred.
routes.remedy: Existing allocation decision is go/no-go and section 7(a) describes revocable access. Proposed withholding of a new allocation pending evidence is narrower than cancelling existing access; a safety-triggered suspension procedure, repayment and provider enforcement still need explicit terms and authority confirmation.
routes.window: Published workflow receives requests on days 1–25 and publishes decisions the following month. The portal was updated 14 October 2026. November 2026–May 2027 approval cycles are a prospective pilot opportunity, not a confirmed safety-policy revision schedule; verify actual committee dates and current terms first.
routes.evidenceSummary: The policy assigns IndiaAI policy updates and PMEC subsidised-request approval. The live portal describes application, subsidy and provider billing. Section 4.6 says 0–50% subsidy but 5.2 says maximum 40%; neither ceiling is silently treated as settled or as covered compute.
routes.gap: No adopted safety schedule, executed provider flow-down, current award ledger or matched GPU-hour totals obtained. Existing anti-misuse controls do not establish frontier-model evaluation obligations.
routes.nextQuestion: Will IndiaAI identify one forthcoming allocation cohort, resolve the subsidy-policy conflict and supply the operative allocation/provider terms plus GPU-hour ledger for a prospective safety pilot?
incentives: Proposed benefit: IndiaAI can show whether subsidised workloads deliver auditable safety evidence.
Proposed benefit: users and providers obtain a predictable review timetable and explicit evidence requirements.
constraints: Users can choose unsubsidised or other compute; reach is limited to the defined allocations.
A new condition needs lawful prospective adoption and provider/user implementation.
GPU counts, subsidy percentages and GPU-hours are different denominators.

sources.claim: IndiaAI updates the policy; PMEC approves subsidised requests on a recurring cycle. Sections 4.6 and 5.2 conflict on the subsidy ceiling. Security/anti-misuse checks and revocable access are specified.

sources.claim: Public application interface describes PMEC approval, provider billing and 30-day approval validity; no authenticated allocation ledger was accessed.

brief: Test safety at the compute-allocation gate
Pilot an evaluation condition on a new cohort of IndiaAI subsidised workloads.
The approval mechanism exists; the safety term and measured compute coverage do not yet.

agreements.scope: One prospective allocation above 5,000 GPU-hours to an already-verified private end-user, implemented through one empanelled cloud provider; not all IndiaAI users or national compute.

actors.name: IndiaAI / Digital India Corporation
actors.role: Adopt prospective terms and approve the allocation; PMEC is an internal approval role, not another institution.
actors.note: Policy responsibility is documented; exact safety approval and contemporaneous leadership support are unverified.

actors.name: Selected end-user company (not yet identified)
actors.role: Accept evidence, deployment and incident duties; supply evaluation results.
actors.note: Can decline the proposed terms; no participant has been selected.

actors.name: Selected empanelled cloud provider (not yet identified)
actors.role: Supply metering and implement any agreed workload suspension.
actors.note: Billing/service relationship is documented, but the proposed enforcement obligation requires its terms.

agreements.limitations: Three-institution allocation/service path implies at least two interfaces, not two approvals already obtained. Procurement amendment and oversight requirements remain unresolved. Proposed measurement: metered GPU-hours under signed safety allocations divided by all metered GPU-hours in the same eligible pilot cohort and period, stratified by accelerator type. Neither count is available. No subsidy ceiling or announced fleet size substitutes for this fraction.

routes.title: Make Dubai's agentic-service deployment assurance a testable safety gate
routes.impactRationale: Unscored new candidate; legacy numbers are compatibility placeholders and must not be shown.
routes.feasibilityRationale: Unscored new candidate; legacy numbers are compatibility placeholders and must not be shown.
routes.actor: Dubai Future Foundation through DCAI, with the participating Dubai government service owner and Digital Dubai/security partners.
routes.obligor: Selected AI implementation company and public service owner for one accelerator deployment.
routes.instrument: Agentic AI for Government Services Accelerator's Build-to-Deploy assurance process; proposed signed pilot acceptance schedule setting pass/fail and rollback conditions.
routes.safeguard: Before live use, test unauthorised tool calls, prompt-injection data extraction and irreversible actions; require human approval for high-consequence actions, version-change retesting, incident records and a tested rollback. These concrete thresholds are proposed, not existing published accelerator rules.
routes.verification: Proposed independent review of a fixed test suite and service logs, including a seeded failure that must block live deployment. By 21–22 June 2027, retain the signed acceptance decision, one completed retest and a timed rollback drill.
routes.remedy: Proposed failed-test consequence: withhold pilot acceptance or revert to the human service channel. Published independent assurance does not itself prove a contractual payment hold, regulator veto or power to stop a supplier's wider model release.
routes.window: Launched 5 October 2026; programme page describes year-round operation and open applications. Use a November 2026–May 2027 service-design or pre-deployment review if a host accepts. Individual pilot dates and procurement commitments are unverified.
routes.evidenceSummary: The programme expressly places independent assurance in deployment. The launch identifies an initial 33 government entities and more than 300 use cases for assessment, not deployments already covered by a new safeguard. October leadership statements favour responsible deployment, not this exact safety schedule.
routes.gap: No pilot contract, named independent assurer, acceptance authority or tested service inventory retrieved. This is Dubai scope within the UAE, not federal procurement power.
routes.nextQuestion: Which service owner can supply a pre-deployment acceptance schedule, identify the final go/no-go signatory and agree to a deliberately failed safety test before scaling?
incentives: Proposed benefit: service owners gain reproducible evidence before exposing residents to autonomous actions.
Proposed benefit: suppliers can demonstrate reliable deployment using a reusable assurance pack.
constraints: Fast deployment incentives can conflict with meaningful failed-test consequences.
Partner participation does not establish a separate veto for every organisation.
The programme's AI Seal priority is not evidence of a frontier-model safety certification.

Add explicit pass/fail tests to a Dubai accelerator service's deployment assurance.
A real programme and timely leadership signals exist; signed safety acceptance terms remain missing.

agreements.scope: One Dubai accelerator service, not nationwide AI regulation; partner endorsement is distinguished from an indispensable approval.

actors.name: Dubai Future Foundation / DCAI
actors.role: Programme sponsor and proposed assurance-schedule convenor.
actors.note: October launch supports accelerated adoption; that ambition alone is not support for a binding fail gate. No separate DCAI institution is counted.

actors.name: Selected Dubai government service owner (not yet identified)
actors.role: Own operational deployment, acceptance and rollback decision.
actors.note: Required operational counterparty; exact authorised signatory and acceptance power need the pilot terms.

actors.name: Selected AI implementation company (not yet identified)
actors.role: Accept evidence access and implement corrections and rollback.
actors.note: A supplier may reject scope, evaluation access or cost. No signed schedule located.

agreements.limitations: The proposed path requires programme sponsor, service owner and vendor, but exact signatures are unverified, so no handoff count is claimed. Digital Dubai/DESC directly support responsible use and lifecycle security in the October launch; they are not counted as independent veto institutions without authority evidence. Independent review may be internal. Proposed coverage: live accelerator services with signed and passed safety acceptance divided by all live services in the same cohort at the cutoff. Candidate use cases and participating entities are incompatible denominators; no matched counts obtained.

routes.title: Write an AI failure stop-rule into a Saudi CST sandbox testing plan
routes.impactRationale: Unscored new candidate; legacy numbers are compatibility placeholders and must not be shown.
routes.feasibilityRationale: Unscored new candidate; legacy numbers are compatibility placeholders and must not be shown.
routes.actor: Communications, Space and Technology Commission (CST), for a qualifying AI-enabled service within its jurisdiction.
routes.obligor: One admitted sandbox company testing an AI-enabled digital service.
routes.instrument: CST Sandbox Application Guidelines sections 4.2–4.4, 5 and 7.1: mutually agreed testing plan, safeguards, acceptance conditions and breach consequences.
routes.safeguard: Proposed AI-specific schedule: limit exposed users, prohibit autonomous high-consequence tool actions, record model changes, and stop the test after a confirmed unauthorised disclosure or action until corrective retesting passes.
routes.verification: Proposed: add model-version and incident fields to monthly reports and preregister failure thresholds. Reconcile exposed transactions and stop events with logs; by 21–22 June 2027 demonstrate one contained failure, pause and verified correction, even if graduation remains pending.
routes.remedy: Guidelines provide corrective measures for minor breaches and possible termination for significant breaches. Applying those outcomes to the proposed AI-specific threshold requires an agreed plan; this is not a nationwide AI deployment ban.
routes.window: Guidelines specify rolling admission; the registration service remains published on 31 October 2026. Late-2026 onboarding or 2027 plan finalisation is a possible route, subject to confirmation of capacity. A fresh applicant cannot be promised graduation by June: published stages include 1–3 months admission, 1–2 preparation and 6–9 testing.
routes.evidenceSummary: An actual regulator-participant instrument defines KPIs, safeguards and breach handling. AI is among eligible technologies, but the service must fall within CST scope. Current registration requirements include a testing and exit plan.
routes.gap: No identified eligible AI participant, signed plan or live intake confirmation. Other regulators may be necessary for a particular use case; CST cannot waive their requirements by assumption.
routes.nextQuestion: Can CST identify an eligible AI service approaching plan agreement and show the signed threshold, reporting template and authority for a safety-triggered pause?
incentives: Proposed benefit: the participant obtains a bounded route to regulatory learning and market readiness.
Proposed benefit: CST obtains measurable failure evidence before wider customer exposure.
constraints: Only sandbox participants and CST-jurisdiction services are reached.
Limited live exposure cannot establish safety of nationwide scaling or the underlying general-purpose model.
A June checkpoint should test operation of the rule, not require an implausibly accelerated full lifecycle.

Use CST's sandbox testing plan to specify an AI failure threshold and corrective retest.
The regulator has a sandbox remedy; the company, AI-specific terms and intake timing need confirmation.

agreements.scope: One CST-jurisdiction sandbox service with no assumed sectoral waiver; application-specific additional authorities remain unresolved.

actors.name: Communications, Space and Technology Commission
actors.role: Agree the plan, admit the participant and decide corrective or termination outcomes.
actors.note: Published procedure establishes the role, not contemporary leadership approval of this AI stop-rule.

actors.name: Selected sandbox company (not yet identified)
actors.role: Accept restrictions, provide test evidence and implement pause/correction.
actors.note: Agreement and participation are voluntary; no exact consent obtained.

agreements.limitations: The documented bilateral plan supplies one minimum interface. Additional sector regulators, data permissions and operational suppliers depend on the selected service. Proposed coverage: logged AI transactions subject to the signed stop-rule divided by all logged AI transactions in that sandbox service and period; report separately from the share of Saudi AI activity. Neither numerator nor denominator is available.

routes.title: Add a safety evidence work package to a TÜBİTAK 1711 consortium agreement
routes.impactRationale: Unscored new candidate; legacy numbers are compatibility placeholders and must not be shown.
routes.feasibilityRationale: Unscored new candidate; legacy numbers are compatibility placeholders and must not be shown.
routes.actor: TÜBİTAK through TEYDEB and its Artificial Intelligence Institute (YZE), with the customer-led 1711 consortium.
routes.obligor: Customer enterprise, SME technology provider and university/research institution in one eligible consortium.
routes.instrument: Updated 1711-YZE-2026 call: cooperation agreement at section 15.2, expenditure review/payment at section 5 and monitoring at section 14. Proposed negotiated safety work package before project-contract signature, if permissible for that selected application.
routes.safeguard: Add a separately costed misuse/failure evaluation, incident-reporting and corrective-retest deliverable to the funded AI solution. Define test access and evidence-sharing rights in the cooperation agreement, with customer acceptance contingent on resolving specified critical failures.
routes.verification: Proposed: university/research partner supplies reproducible test evidence for the customer's intended use; YZE/TEYDEB review it through the project-monitoring process. By 21–22 June 2027 obtain signed terms and one interim test/retest package, rather than claim a completed 24-month project.
routes.remedy: Proposed customer non-acceptance and correction of a failed safety deliverable must be written into the agreement. Existing eligible-expenditure review does not automatically authorise clawback for a failed safety test; the programme FAQ says ordinary project failure does not trigger repayment.
routes.window: The extended 2026 application deadline was 2 October 2026, 23:59: CLOSED. Updated section 15.2 permits the cooperation agreement to be signed by project-contract signature, creating a conditional late-2026/2027 negotiation opportunity only if a selected project remains unsigned. No award/signature dates or 2027 call dates verified.
routes.evidenceSummary: The updated call supplies a concrete agreement, funding and review path. Its signature rule is more specific than the earlier announcement. The programme page describes annual calls, not a confirmed pre-Geneva 2027 opening.
routes.gap: No selected unsigned project, current grant decision or executed agreement located. Adding a material requirement after applications may be impermissible; prospective 2027 terms are a fallback, not a confirmed window.
routes.nextQuestion: Is any selected 2026 project still before signature, and would TÜBİTAK permit an agreed safety work package without changing the competitive award basis?
incentives: Proposed benefit: customers receive evidence that the AI solution is fit for their specific deployment.
Proposed benefit: grant-funded providers and researchers can budget evaluation and clarification of evidence rights.
constraints: All consortium partners must accept costs, evaluation access and intellectual-property terms.
Funding commercial application development does not imply control over upstream frontier-model releases.
The next routine half-year period ends 30 June 2027, after Geneva; request an interim checkpoint rather than promise that final period report.
